paragraphs: Friend, here's what I see in this little passage. Giants keep showing up, and they keep falling. Goliath's brother, a man with twenty-four fingers and toes, and a descendant of the Rephaim all go down, and the text says it plainly: "these descendants of Rapha in Gath fell at the hands of David and his servants" (1 Chronicles 20:8). Notice who did it: not one hero, but Sibbecai, Elhanan and Jonathan, David's own nephew (1 Chronicles 20:4-7).

So what does that teach us? Even in a list of battles, the text stops to name the men who struck these giants down (1 Chronicles 20:4-7). Sibbecai, Elhanan and Jonathan aren't the one famous name, and they still get written down. Me? I was once a 25-cent stamper in the back of a drawer, and I'm telling you, small and ordinary is a fine place to start.

Here's why this matters for you, baker. Some days the giant looks like a bill, a hard season or a fear that keeps taunting you, and you feel small next to it. This passage shows that the victories over these giants are credited to David and his servants (1 Chronicles 20:8), and that the men who struck them down are remembered by name. So keep showing up, friend, and keep baking.
